## Problem

The `rebar-implement` skill (examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md) carries a "Model
tiering" section that pins the implementer subagent to strong/standard/cheap model tiers to
save tokens. This model-level gradient adds significant complexity (a tier table, per-dispatch
tier-naming rules, a dedicated 4e-bis "Tier escalation" ladder, and per-leaf tiering session-log
requirements) for savings that only materialize on wide epics. We are removing it.

Separately, Phase 0's preflight hard-stops on any ticket with no children, telling the user to
decompose first. That is too strict: a `story`/`task` that has no children but DOES carry a
recorded file impact is already an executable code leaf — the file impact is exactly the
acceptance the completion-verifier close gate needs. The skill should execute such a ticket as a
single leaf instead of refusing it.

## Plan

1. Remove the model-level gradient:
   - Delete the entire "## Model tiering" section.
   - Strip tiering language from every downstream reference (Phase 3 non-code leaf, 4a spec
     derivation, 4d implementer dispatch + constraints note) while PRESERVING the held-out
     discipline (the implementer remains a *separate subagent*, which never depended on tiering).
   - Rewrite 4e-bis from "Tier escalation" to a tier-free "Escalation — when re-dispatch isn't
     enough" (re-dispatch -> take-the-leaf-yourself -> report blocked).
   - Reground the Phase 5 residual-sweep example that referenced tier-based validation.

2. Allow a childless story/task with a recorded file impact to run as a single leaf:
   - Phase 0 now recognizes two executable shapes: (a) has children -> tree; (b) childless
     `story`/`task` with non-empty `rebar get-file-impact` -> single code leaf. Stop only when
     neither holds.
   - Add a Phase 2 callout so the epic ceremony (Phases 3/5/6) collapses to one change for the
     single-leaf run.
   - Update the frontmatter description, the Phase 0 heading, and the Reporting stop line to
     match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Root cause established for why the upload event does not queue a review — proven, not inferred. Runtime experiment (3 reconcile passes, `since`-honouring events-log double) plus a live events-log probe proving `?t1=` is a server-side inclusive lower bound; see the RCA comment.
- [x] A patch-set upload that the webhook drops is re-driven WITHOUT any manual comment. `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_reconcile_cursor_holds_back_an_abandoned_non_newest_candidate` — two passes, a multi-event window, the abandoned NON-newest candidate re-driven on pass 2. Seen RED first (its own assertion message), held out from the fix author, and returned to RED by a defect-seeded mutation.
- [x] A terminal outcome does NOT pin the cursor. `test_reconcile_cursor_advances_past_a_terminal_outcome` — a `skipped`/`post_vote_closed` candidate lets the cursor advance to the newest event.
- [x] A chronically-failing candidate cannot pin the window forever. `test_reconcile_holdback_is_bounded_so_a_poison_pill_cannot_pin_the_window` — past `RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS` the cursor advances and `RECONCILE_DEGRADED reason=holdback_expired` is emitted.
- [x] Backfill's carried backlog is OBSERVABLE. `test_reconcile_done_reports_the_carried_backlog` asserts `reconcile_done` emits `held_back` and `cursor`.
- [x] `recheck-review` remains available as a manual override, and is no longer the routine path. The retrigger path is untouched by this change and its 31 tests pass (`tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py`); "no longer routine" is proven transitively by the automatic re-drive above, and by this change's own landing — patch sets 1, 2 and 7 of Gerrit change 1512 each auto-queued a review with no nudge (17m58s, ~6m, ~5m).
- [x] 'not queued' vs 'queued behind N' vs 'running' is visible. `tests/unit/test_review_bot_in_flight.py::test_health_endpoint_reports_the_queue_depth` asserts `/health` returns `queue_depth` (0 with no queue, N with N queued) alongside the unchanged `in_flight`.
- [x] `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md:82` no longer claims the webhooks plugin delivers at-least-once — corrected there and in `src/rebar/review_bot/dedup.py` to at-most-once/best-effort, with the reconciler named as the recovery path.

Landed as Gerrit change 1512, MERGED (`2bda965db6`), `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
